summary: Markets staged a cautious rebound Monday after last week's brutal tech selloff, with Nasdaq 100 futures climbing 1.9% and chip stocks rallying 3.5% as dip buyers emerged despite lingering doubts about AI spending returns. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh offered no guidance on the upcoming October 27-28 FOMC meeting, driving rate-hike odds down to just 15% and lifting gold toward $4,200 as Treasury yields eased. Inflation remains the key risk: September CPI accelerated to 3.7% year-over-year—the hottest since early 2023—driven by a 9.1% monthly spike in gasoline, while import prices jumped 1.1% on surging fuel costs. Earnings season intensifies this week with Meta and Tesla reporting Wednesday, while crypto held steady above key support levels despite a second consecutive week of Bitcoin ETF outflows totaling $229 million. Oil hovered near $110 on Middle East supply risks, mortgage rates topped 7.2%, and the New York Fed's Services Index plunged to a seven-month low, signaling mounting stagflation fears as investors brace for a data-heavy, earnings-packed week.

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh offers no October rate guidance as inflation runs at 3.7%
signals.desc: Warsh's refusal to signal policy intent left markets pricing only 15% odds of an October hike despite CPI hitting 3.7% YoY, the highest since 2023, raising stagflation concerns.

signals.title: Nasdaq 100 surges 1.9% as chip stocks rebound 3.5% on AI dip-buying
signals.desc: Tech buyers returned after Friday's 4.5% Nasdaq rout, with Intel upgraded by JPMorgan and CoreWeave rallying 6% on Goldman Sachs upgrade, signaling confidence in AI capex despite recent doubts.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs post $229M outflows for second straight week
signals.desc: Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $228.58 million last week, the second consecutive week of redemptions, though BTC held above $82,000 support amid structural resilience.

signals.title: September CPI jumps 0.6% monthly on 9.1% gasoline spike
signals.desc: Headline inflation accelerated to 3.7% YoY from 3.4%, driven by energy costs that accounted for over half the monthly increase, while core inflation remains elevated at 3.0%.

signals.title: Cleveland-Cliffs surges 12% on Q3 earnings beat ahead of heavy reporting week
signals.desc: Steel producer Cleveland-Cliffs topped Q3 estimates before the open, while Meta, Tesla, Netflix, and 212 firms over $2B market cap report this week, providing earnings catalysts.

verdict: Tech's bounce and lower rate-hike odds provide near-term relief, but sticky 3.7% inflation, heavy earnings tests, and crypto outflows keep risk elevated into a volatile week.
